tagline: Japan's tropical archipelago — 9.66M visitors a year, diving paradises reached only by typhoon-fragile ferries and short-hop flights.
summary: Okinawa is Japan's tropical island economy: Naha and the main island, the Kerama reefs just offshore, and 400 km southwest the Yaeyama group (Ishigaki, Iriomote, Taketomi, Hateruma) — some of the clearest diving water in Asia and a UNESCO-listed wilderness. The prefecture drew 9.66M visitors in 2024. Inside each cluster, island-hopping is dense but runs on exposed, weather-fragile diesel ferries; between clusters, travellers fly. It is a two-scale network — short protected hops within Yaeyama and the Keramas, and a long open-water spine from the main island — that maps cleanly onto Navier's two platforms, with a conservation mandate baked in by UNESCO and national-park status.

demand_signals.label: Okinawa visitor arrivals
demand_signals.note: Third-highest on record, ~95% of pre-pandemic levels; diving, beach-resort and island-hopping tourism.

demand_signals.label: Yaeyama inter-island ferries
demand_signals.note: Ishigaki is the hub for a dense duopoly ferry network (Anei Kanko, Yaeyama Kanko Ferry) to Taketomi, Iriomote, Kohama, Kuroshima, Hateruma — short hops, very high frequency.

demand_signals.label: UNESCO World Heritage wilderness
demand_signals.note: Iriomote/Yanbaru natural World Heritage; Kerama Shoto National Park (2014) protects the reefs off Naha — strong clean-marine mandate over diesel fleets in protected waters.

demand_signals.label: Exposed open-water cancellations
demand_signals.note: Yaeyama and Kerama crossings sit in open ocean; ferries are routinely cancelled or rough on exposed days — the single strongest reliability/comfort demand hook.

demand_signals.label: Main-island ↔ Yaeyama gap
demand_signals.note: No practical surface link between Naha and the Yaeyama group; the ~220 nm open-water spine is flown by Ryukyu Air Commuter / JTA — a natural hybrid line-haul corridor.

use_cases.title: Reliable Yaeyama island-hopping
use_cases.body: A smooth, near-silent foiling network out of Ishigaki to Taketomi, Iriomote, Kohama and Hateruma that keeps running and stays comfortable when exposed-water diesel ferries are rough or cancelled — converting weather-fragility into a reliability premium.

use_cases.title: Kerama reef day-trips from Naha
use_cases.body: Clean, quiet crossings from Naha/Tomari to the Kerama Islands (Tokashiki, Zamami, Aka) — zero-emission service into the protected reef waters of Kerama Shoto National Park, ideal for divers and whale-watchers.

use_cases.title: Resort-island private transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling arrivals to resort jetties across the Yaeyama and main-island hotel strips (Onna-son, Ishigaki, Kohama, Taketomi) — replacing ferry-plus-shuttle chains with one seamless premium hop.

use_cases.title: Main-island ↔ Yaeyama hybrid line-haul
use_cases.body: The ~220 nm open-ocean run from Naha to the Yaeyama group is beyond all-electric range and flown today — a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor that adds a premium surface option with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

journeys.today: Open-water diesel ferry that gets rough — and is cancelled outright on high-wind days, stranding day-trippers.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth, foil-borne crossing that flies above the chop and keeps a reliable schedule when conventional ferries can't sail.

journeys.today: Fast-ferry or slow car-ferry on a fixed timetable; weather-exposed and diesel into a protected reef park.
journeys.with_navier: A clean, near-silent foiling hop straight to the dive islands — zero-emission inside Kerama Shoto National Park.

journeys.today: A long, notoriously rough open-water ferry frequently cancelled — Hateruma is famous for being hard to reach.
journeys.with_navier: A foiling crossing that smooths the most exposed leg in the group, opening Japan's southernmost island to reliable day access.

journeys.today: Air-only — a ~1-hour flight; no surface alternative across the open ocean.
journeys.with_navier: A Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul across the ~220 nm spine, adding a premium sea connection with no charging stop required.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Two distinct intra-cluster meshes are pure Pioneer II territory: the Yaeyama hub network out of Ishigaki (Taketomi ~3.5 nm, Iriomote ~11 nm, Kohama ~14 nm, Hateruma ~33 nm) and the Kerama crossings from Naha/Tomari (~19 nm). All sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope; the value is reliability and comfort on otherwise exposed water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The two clusters are ~220 nm apart across open ocean (Naha ↔ Yaeyama) — far beyond all-electric range and flown today. This is an explicit Quanta-LR hybrid corridor; never imply one continuous all-electric network. Quanta-LR also serves the Naha ↔ Miyako leg (~155 nm) and other inter-island spines with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

competitive_landscape: Within Yaeyama, a two-operator ferry duopoly (Anei Kanko, Yaeyama Kanko Ferry) runs a dense, high-frequency diesel network from Ishigaki; the Kerama Islands are served by fast and car ferries from Naha/Tomari (Marine Liner Tokashiki, Queen Zamami). Between clusters, Ryukyu Air Commuter and JTA carry the long Naha↔Yaeyama and Naha↔Miyako flows by air. The frequency and load prove a mature island-hopping market — but the inter-island legs are exposed, weather-fragile and diesel, and there is no clean or premium on-demand option. Cancellations and rough crossings on typhoon-season and winter-monsoon days are the clearest demand evidence.

precedents.why_it_matters: A $100M, ~100-vessel phased electric-foiling network proves the two-platform (inner-atoll electric + long-haul hybrid) model at national scale — directly analogous to Okinawa's short-cluster + long-spine geometry.

seasonality: Two overlapping exposure windows define the year: the typhoon season (roughly Jun–Oct) and the NE winter monsoon (Nov–Mar), both of which bring rough seas and ferry cancellations to the open-water Yaeyama and Kerama crossings. This weather-fragility is the core demand hook — a foil-borne hull flies above the chop for a smoother, more reliable ride precisely when conventional ferries struggle or stop. Calmest diving conditions are late spring and early autumn between the windows.
regulatory_note: Operates under Japan Coast Guard (JCG 11th Regional HQ, Naha) and MLIT Kyushu oversight. Iriomote sits within a UNESCO natural World Heritage site (2021) and the Kerama reefs within Kerama Shoto National Park (2014) — a clean-marine mandate where displacing diesel-ferry emissions in protected, biodiverse waters is concrete sourced demand evidence. Quiet-mode operation also matters near the Iriomote wildcat habitat and humpback whale-watching grounds. Aligns with Japan's 2050 carbon-neutrality and MLIT zero-emission-vessel programmes.
signature_routes: Ishigaki ↔ Taketomi / Iriomote / Kohama / Hateruma (Yaeyama foiling mesh, all-electric)
Naha / Tomari ↔ Kerama Islands (zero-emission reef-park crossings)
Naha ↔ Ishigaki (~220 nm main-island ↔ Yaeyama hybrid spine, Quanta-LR)
Naha ↔ Miyako (~155 nm hybrid line-haul, Quanta-LR)
